memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You are to undergo circumcision, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and you. For the generations to come every male among you who is eight days old must be circumcised, including those born in your household or bought with money from foreigners..." - Gen 17:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God is careful to include everyone in the covenant sign - not just Abraham's biological children, but "those born in your household or bought with money from foreigners." The servants, the outsiders, the ones acquired from other nations - all were to receive the sign. From the very beginning, God's covenant reached beyond bloodlines to embrace those who were not born into the family.

This is a beautiful hint of God's wider heart. Even in a covenant given to one family, God makes room for the foreigner, the outsider, the one brought in from elsewhere. His purposes were never meant to be narrow. The stranger could belong.

Notice too the emphasis on "the generations to come." God was thinking not just of Abraham but of the children and grandchildren and great-grandchildren who would follow. The covenant sign was to be passed down, a faith handed carefully from one generation to the next.

Both of these threads reach their fulfilment in Christ. The gospel gathers in the outsider - "you who once were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ" (Eph 2:13) - and it is to be passed down, for "the promise is for you and your children and for all who are far off" (Acts 2:39). God's covenant family was always meant to grow outward and forward. Are you helping bring in the outsider and pass faith to the next generation?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you helping bring outsiders into God's family?
- Are you passing faith on to the next generation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that Your covenant reaches beyond bloodlines to the outsider and forward to the generations. Help me welcome those who are far off and faithfully pass on my faith to those who come after me.
Amen.
